scope: Six representative reactions from three user-supplied articles and their SI (251 PDF pages); not a complete substrate-scope extraction.

reactions.name: Nicewicz · Aldehyde α-alkylation · Table 1 entry 3

conditions.Scale: diethyl bromomalonate 0.385 mmol (1.0 equiv); aldehyde 0.769 mmol (2.0 equiv)
conditions.Yield basis: Isolated yield from the SI; article discrepancy unresolved

evidence.quote: General Procedure: An oven-dried 8 mL vial equipped with a Teflon septum and magnetic stir bar was charged with tris-(2,2´-bipyridyl)ruthenium (II) chloride hexahydrate (1.9 µmol, 0.005 equiv), the corresponding bromide (0.385 mmol, 1.0 equiv), and (2R,5S)-2-tert-butyl-3,5-dimethylimidazolidin-4-one trifluoromethane- sulfonic acid salt (76.9 µmol, 0.2 equiv). The vial was purged with a stream of nitrogen and 0.8 mL of dry DMF was added via syringe, followed by the corresponding aldehyde (0.769 mmol, 2.0 equiv) and 2,6-lutidine (0.769 mmol, 2.0 equiv). The resultant mixture was degassed for 10 min by bubbling nitrogen through the reaction medium. After the reaction was thoroughly degassed, the vial was sealed with parafilm and placed approximately 8 cm from a 15 W fluorescent lamp. After the reaction was complete (as judged by TLC analysis), the mixture was poured into a separatory funnel containing 5 mL of Et2O and 5 mL of H2O. The layers were separated and the aqueous layer was extracted with Et2O (3 × 5 mL). The combined organic layers were dried (MgSO4) and concentrated in vacuo. Purification of the crude product by flash chromatography on Davisil Grade 643 silica gel using the indicated solvent system afforded the desired α- alkylated aldehyde.
evidence.locator: General Procedure; light source, solvent and nitrogen atmosphere

evidence.quote: (R)-Diethyl 2-(1-oxo-3-phenylpropan-2-yl)propanedioate (entry 3, Table 1):
evidence.locator: Entry 3 name and structure; visually checked

evidence.quote: bipyridyl)ruthenium (II) chloride hexahydrate (1.9 µmol, 0.005 equiv), 66.0 µL of diethyl bromomalonate (0.385 mmol, 1.0 equiv), 24.6 mg of (2R,5S)-2-tert-butyl-3,5- dimethylimidazolidin-4-one trifluoromethanesulfonic acid salt (76.9 µmol, 0.2 equiv), 101 µL of hydrocinnamaldehyde (0.769 mmol, 2.0 equiv), and 90.0 µL 2,6-lutidine (0.769 mmol, 2.0 equiv). After 7 h, the reaction mixture was subjected to the workup protocol outlined in the general procedure and purified by flash chromatography using petroleum ether:Et2O (4:1) as the eluent to afford 105 mg (93% yield, 91% ee) of the title compound as a colorless oil.

The yield field uses the SI value; values are not combined or averaged. 23 °C is from the article scheme. The separate 465 nm/500 mW control experiment does not apply. reactions.name: Zuo · Decarboxylative arylation · p-tolyl (10)
reactions.reagents: Ir[dF(CF₃)ppy]₂(dtbbpy)PF₆ 0.01 equiv; NiCl₂·glyme 0.10 equiv; dtbbpy 0.15 equiv; Cs₂CO₃ 1.5 equiv

conditions.Scale: aryl halide 0.40 mmol (1.0 equiv); Boc-Pro-OH 0.60 mmol (1.5 equiv)

evidence.quote: General Procedure A for the Decarboxylative Arylation (Arene Scope): An oven- dried 40 mL vial equipped with a Teflon septum and magnetic stir bar was charged with Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 (4.00 μmol, 0.01 equiv), NiCl2glyme (0.04 mmol, 0.1 equiv), 4,4-di-tert-butyl-2,2-bipyridyl (0.06 mmol, 0.15 equiv), the corresponding aromatic halides (0.40 mmol, 1.0 equiv), Boc-Pro-OH (0.60 mmol, 1.5 equiv), Cs2CO3 (0.60 mmol, 1.5 equiv), and 20 mL of DMF. The reaction mixture was degassed by bubbling argon stream for 20 min, then irradiated with two 26 W fluorescent lamps (at approximately 2 cm away from the light source). After 72h, the reaction mixture was diluted with saturated aqueous NaHCO3 solution, extracted with Et2O (3 × 100 mL). The combined organic extracts were washed with water and brine, dried over MgSO4 and concentrated in vacuo. Purification of the crude product by flash chromatography on silica gel using the indicated solvent system afforded the desired product.
evidence.locator: S5, General Procedure A; separate from Procedure B

evidence.quote: tert-Butyl 2-(p-tolyl)pyrrolidine-1-carboxylate [known compound (27)]: According to the general procedure A, Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 (4.5 mg, 4.0 μmol, 0.01 equiv), NiCl2glyme (8.8 mg, 0.04 mmol, 0.1 equiv), 4,4-di-tert-butyl-2,2-bipyridyl (16.1 mg, 0.06 mmol, 0.15 equiv), 4-iodotoluene (89.0 mg, 0.4 mmol, 1.0 equiv), Boc-Pro-OH (129.0 mg, 0.60 mmol, 1.5 equiv), Cs2CO3 (195.6 mg, 0.6 mmol, 1.5 equiv), and 20 mL of DMF were used. The product was isolated by flash chromatography (15% ethyl acetate/hexane) as a pale yellow solid (81 mg, 78%).
evidence.locator: S7, individual synthesis; product structure and formula checked

evidence.quote: Fig. 3. Photoredox-nickel catalyzed decarboxylative cross-coupling: aryl halide scope.
evidence.locator: Fig. 3; 23 °C and racemic (±)-10, (±)-14 checked visually

reactions.notes: Checked against SI General Procedure A, S7 and racemic (±)-10 in article Fig. 3. The 34 W blue LED belongs to Procedure B. Decarboxylation byproducts including CO2 are omitted from the graph. Record review does not establish experimental reproducibility.

reactions.name: Horn · Electrochemical allylic oxidation · tert-butyl (6)
reactions.reagents: Cl₄NHPI 0.2 equiv; pyridine 2.0 equiv; 70% aqueous tBuOOH 1.5 equiv

conditions.Atmosphere: No special measures to exclude air or moisture (small-scale procedure)
conditions.Cell setup: Glass slide between RVC anode and cathode
conditions.Current per substrate amount: 10 mA/mmol substrate; not current density per electrode area
conditions.Endpoint: Until complete by TLC or GCMS; no fixed reaction time reported
conditions.Solvent: MeCN 3 mL — explicit substrate-specific exception to acetone

evidence.quote: General Procedure for Electrochemical Allylic Oxidation: With no precautions to exclude air or moisture, a test tube is charged with a stir bar, Cl4NHPI (0.2 equiv.) and LiClO4 (0.6 equiv, 0.1 M). Acetone (6 mL/mmol substrate) is added, and the resulting suspension is stirred until most of the solids dissolve. Substrate (1 equiv.) is added, followed by pyridine (2 equiv.) and 70% aqueous tert-butyl hydroperoxide (1.5 equiv.). The anode and cathode (RVC, separated by a glass slide) are placed in the solution, and the reaction mixture is electrolyzed at a current of 10 mA/mmol substrate until the reaction is complete WWW.NATURE.COM/NATURE | 6
evidence.locator: Small-scale general procedure; 10 mA/mmol and RVC anode/cathode

evidence.quote: as judged by TLC or GCMS analysis. The reaction mixture is transferred to a separatory funnel, and the electrodes are washed thoroughly with hexanes, diethyl ether, or ethyl acetate. The organic layer is washed twice with H2O, once with brine, dried, and concentrated. The resulting crude product was then purified on SiO2 to furnish the desired enone product.
evidence.locator: Small-scale endpoint and purification; separate from large-scale procedure

evidence.quote: tert-Butyl cyclohexenone (6). Following the general procedure Me Me with 0.5 mmol tert-butyl cyclohexene (69 mg) using MeCN (3 mL) Me in place of acetone afforded the title compound (40 mg, 52% yield) O as a clear, colorless oil after purification on SiO2 (5% Et2O/hexanes).
evidence.locator: Compound 6; MeCN exception, 52% yield and structure checked visually

reactions.notes: The explicit MeCN exception on SI PDF p. 45 replaces general acetone conditions. 10 mA/mmol is current per substrate amount, not mA/cm². Large-scale graphite, LiBF4 and 5 mA/mmol conditions do not apply. Fixed time, charge and area-based current density are unreported. No independent experimental reproduction.
